dedupe_keys.name: local soy value chains in northern ghana netlogo model for evaluating value chain development interventions

description: This NetLogo model evaluates alternative interventions by a value chain development programme in northern Ghana, where distrust between partners can stop soy value chains from working. It was written by Tim Verwaart and published in the CoMSES library in 2019 (version 1.0.0). The programme supports bringing smallholder farmers into soy clusters or agricultural APEX organisations, which are farmers' cooperatives, within a fair business environment; the aim is to include smallholders in a strong value chain and reduce distrust, improving rural livelihoods and food and nutrition security. The code is available as a free download from CoMSES under the GPL-2.0 licence. Caveats: it is tied to one programme, and the page gives no data or validation. Coverage is northern Ghana. Simulation uses: comparing interventions that stabilise local food supply chains in low-income regions. Related records: the Meru County sorghum model (model-comses-sorghum-supply-meru-kenya), by the same author, treats a similar processor and smallholder chain in Kenya.
inputs: Smallholder farmers, soy clusters and APEX farmer organisations
